claims.text: The baseline material is as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
Introducing a lattice or cellular architecture into HfMoTaTiZr will reduce its bulk density.
The proposed density reduction arises from introducing voids or hollow structures.
A lattice or cellular HfMoTaTiZr architecture can maintain mechanical strength despite its reduced bulk density.
The architecture will maintain or only slightly reduce room-temperature mechanical strength relative to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
The architecture will maintain or only slightly reduce elevated-temperature mechanical strength relative to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
The proposed performance is applicable at temperatures up to approximately 1000 °C.
The applicable loading regime does not exceed the yield strength of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
The density and mechanical performance should be compared with an as-cast HfMoTaTiZr control at room temperature and 1000 °C.
A density reduction of less than 5% relative to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr would falsify the hypothesis.
A strength reduction greater than 10% at room temperature would falsify the hypothesis.
A strength reduction greater than 10% at 1000 °C would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says density can be reduced without sacrificing mechanical properties, whereas the predicted outcome allows slightly reduced strength and the falsification rule accepts strength losses of up to 10%.
